note: Reference boards for characters (NPCs), clothing, shops, streets and vehicles along the Dammam -> Latakia road, set in the 2000s. 'commons' = Wikimedia Commons search queries loaded live on the site (filterable to photos taken 2000-2009). 'search' = keywords for outside searches (Flickr/Google/YouTube), 'ar' = Arabic keywords. 'notes' = era notes for the game; general observations to check against the photos, not rules.

boards.title: Saudi men – thobe, ghutra, shemagh
boards.title_ar: لباس الرجال في السعودية – ثوب وشماغ وغترة
notes: White thobe in summer; heavier, darker thobes (grey, brown, navy) in the cold northern winter (Arar, Turaif).
Red-and-white shemagh most common in the north; plain white ghutra also worn. Black igal on top; younger men often without igal.
Sandals (na'al) everyday; bisht (cloak) only for formal occasions.
Workers and drivers: thobe or trousers + shirt; many expatriate workers in work overalls.

boards.title: Saudi women – abaya, niqab
boards.title_ar: لباس النساء في السعودية – عباية ونقاب
notes: In the 2000s women in public almost always wore a black abaya; in the conservative north often the 'abaya over the head' style with face covered (niqab or full veil).
Women did not drive in Saudi Arabia then: female NPCs travel as passengers with family, usually in the back seat of a GMC / Land Cruiser / Suburban.
Family sections in restaurants; women rarely at roadside tea stands or fuel kiosks.

boards.title: Bedouin herders & desert families
boards.search: Bedouin camel herder northern Saudi Arabia
boards.ar: بدو رعاة إبل الشمال بيت شعر
notes: Black goat-hair tent (bayt al-sha'r) or, by the 2000s, often a white canvas tent + pickup truck + water tanker.
Herders drive Toyota Hilux / Land Cruiser pickups; camels moved in trucks.
Bedouin women in Jordan: dark embroidered dresses, head cover; older women may have traditional face tattoos.

boards.title: Jordanians – street & rural clothing
notes: Red-and-white shemagh (Jordanian) very common, often with Western clothes (trousers, jacket).
Women: mix of hijab with long coat (jilbab/manto), some uncovered in towns; Bedouin dress in the Badia.
Army / police uniforms visible at checkpoints and borders.

boards.title: Syrians – city, village and coast
notes: Very mixed styles in the 2000s: Western clothes in cities; women with hijab + long manto coat, some with no headscarf, especially on the coast (Latakia, Tartus).
Older village women: white or dark headscarves, long dresses. Older men: keffiyeh, sometimes sirwal trousers.
Young men: jeans, leather jackets, gelled hair, Nokia phones.

boards.title: Travellers – families, students, workers on the road
boards.search: Syrian families travel Gulf summer car roof luggage
boards.ar: مسافرين من الخليج إلى سوريا صيفاً عفش على السيارة
notes: Classic summer image: a family car (GMC, Caprice, Land Cruiser) with luggage tied high on the roof rack, heading from the Gulf to Syria/Jordan.
Syrian & Jordanian workers in Saudi Arabia going home for holidays; long lines at Al-Haditha and Nassib in summer.
Long-distance buses (e.g. SAPTCO, Syrian and Jordanian coach companies) with passengers carrying bags and blankets.
Women and children travel with male relatives; families stop at fuel stations for prayer and food.

boards.title: Truck drivers & truck stops
boards.search: truck drivers Saudi Jordan border queue
notes: Many drivers from Syria, Jordan, Egypt, Pakistan, India; sleeping in the cab or on a mat beside the truck.
Trucks: Mercedes-Benz (Actros and older), Volvo, MAN, Scania; decorated cabs with curtains, stickers, fringe.
Truck stops = gravel lots + workshop + restaurant + mosque/musalla + tea.

boards.title: Traveller stops – pray, sleep, eat, restrooms
boards.title_ar: محطات الطريق – صلاة ونوم وأكل ودورات مياه
boards.search: Saudi highway rest stop mosque restaurant trucks
boards.ar: استراحة طريق مسجد محطة مطعم شاحنات نوم
notes: Prayer: almost every station has a small mosque or musalla with a minaret or loudspeaker and an ablution area (row of taps); travellers stop at prayer times, shops may close briefly.

Sleep: truck drivers sleep in the cab or on a mat next to the truck; families use simple roadside rooms ('furnished apartments' / motels) or push on to the next town; some rest on carpets in the open at rest areas.
Eat: cheap restaurants with rice & chicken, kabsa, ful, bread, tea in small glasses and Arabic coffee; plastic chairs, fluorescent tubes, a TV on the wall.
Restrooms: basic, often behind the mosque or station building, separate for men and women.
Checkpoints: police/army checkpoints on the highways and before borders – slow down, show ID (iqama/passport), car papers checked.

boards.title: Fuel stations & roadside complexes
boards.ar: محطة بنزين طريق سريع السعودية قديمة
notes: 2000s Saudi road stations: often basic – pumps under a canopy, a small grocery (bakala), a cheap restaurant, a musalla and toilets; tyre repair shop next door.
Station names painted on walls; Arabic-only signs common outside big cities.
Fuel was extremely cheap; attendants (often expatriates) fill the tank – no self-service.

boards.title: Small shops – bakala, tea, shawarma, tyre repair
notes: Bakala: shelves of Pepsi/Mirinda cans, chips, phone cards (Sawa cards), cigarettes, water bottles; fridges with glass doors.
'Bneshar' (tyre repair) shops with stacks of tyres outside.
Restaurants: plastic chairs, fluorescent lights, menu boards with photos; kabsa, chicken, ful, tea in small glasses.

boards.title: Syrian souqs & street vendors
boards.ar: سوق الحميدية بائع عرق سوس دمشق
notes: Street vendors: juice (erk sous / licorice) sellers with brass jugs, ka'ak bread sellers, vegetable carts.
Shop signs hand-painted or plastic; portraits and flags common on walls in the 2000s.
Coastal towns: fish markets, cafés with narghile.

boards.title: Street & road scenes
notes: Wide streets, sodium street lights, low concrete buildings painted beige/white, shop rows under arcades.
Road signs bilingual on highways (blue/green); camel-warning signs on the Tapline Road.
Watch for 2000s details: Nokia/Ericsson ads, Pepsi signs, old phone booths, satellite dishes on every roof.

boards.title: 2000s cars, pickups & buses
boards.search: Saudi cars 2000s GMC Land Cruiser Caprice
boards.ar: سيارات السعودية ٢٠٠٥ جمس شاص لاندكروزر كابرس
notes: Saudi road: Land Cruiser (80/100 series), GMC Suburban/Yukon, Chevrolet Caprice, Toyota Camry, Hilux pickups ('shas' / 'hilux' for herders), Datsun pickups.
Jordan: many older Mercedes taxis, Hyundai/Kia, yellow taxis.
Syria: old American cars and Peugeots, Kia/Hyundai, white 'microbus' minibuses (Suzuki/Hyundai), Pullman coaches.

boards.title: Tapline stations & company towns
boards.search: Tapline pump station Badanah Rafha Turaif
boards.ar: خط التابلاين محطة بدنة رفحاء طريف
notes: By the 2000s the pipeline had stopped pumping (Saudi part shut down in the 1980s–1990), so station compounds were partly abandoned or reused – good mood for Arar_Station.
Fenced compounds, staff houses, water towers, rusting pipe segments along the road.

boards.title: Border posts & queues
boards.search: Haditha border crossing queue Jordan Saudi
boards.ar: منفذ الحديثة طابور العمري جابر نصيب
notes: Long queues of family cars and trucks, especially in summer; officers in uniform, customs inspection of luggage.
Money changers, insurance kiosks, duty-free shops, tea sellers walking between cars.
